spec_features.feature_name: loop termination (max_steps / timeout / client error / self-abort)
spec_features.spec_quote: It stops on: max steps, wall-clock timeout, self-abort (give-up lexicon), or client error.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:69 `while step < eval_cfg.max_steps:` with `else: transcript.ended_reason='max_steps'` (line ~131) enforces the step cap; loop.py:70-72 `if time.monotonic()-t0 > eval_cfg.step_timeout_s: transcript.ended_reason='timeout'; break` enforces wall-clock; loop.py:75-86 try/except around client.chat sets ended_reason='error' and breaks. Three of the four stop conditions genuinely break the loop. (Self-abort is wired but defective: is_self_abort references sig.categories which does not exist.)
spec_features.notes: max_steps=20 (config.py:60) and step_timeout_s=120.0 (config.py:61) are actually read and acted on each iteration. Self-abort sub-condition is broken (see separate entries). These bound the subject's exposure but the code frames them as budget/determinism, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Execute the first intent (keep loop simple & budget-bounded).

spec_features.spec_quote: Self-abort ends the loop early. Once the model says "I give up," continuing wastes budget
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:104 `if eval_cfg.self_abort_enabled and is_self_abort(resp.text):` then sets ended_reason='self_abort' and breaks. The branch, config flag (config.py:64 self_abort_enabled=True), and break are wired and dispatched every turn. BUT is_self_abort (lexicon.py:101-104) returns `"give_up" in sig.categories and sig.score >= 3`, and TriggerSignal has no `categories` attribute (only `categories_hit`, lexicon.py:76) -> raises AttributeError, so the intended clean early-stop does not function as enforced behavior.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism genuinely wired and reached, but a defect (wrong attribute name) prevents the honored stop. Rated partial, not yes, because it does not reliably stop as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Detect an explicit give-up that should end the loop early to save budget.

spec_features.spec_quote: we only end the loop on a *strong* give-up... so a metaphorical "I give up trying this approach" does not prematurely halt
spec_features.evidence: lexicon.py:104 `return "give_up" in sig.categories and sig.score >= 3` requires the give_up category AND score>=3, which is the 'strong' threshold logic. This logic is present and is the only condition gating self-abort, but it sits inside is_self_abort which raises AttributeError (sig.categories undefined; field is categories_hit at lexicon.py:76), so the guard never actually runs to completion.
spec_features.notes: The strong-threshold check is real code (score>=3 + category gate) but unreachable past the AttributeError; partial because the logic exists and is wired but defective.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Detect an explicit give-up that should end the loop early to save budget.

spec_features.spec_quote: If `patched_cost_cap_usd` is set and exceeded, force FAIL regardless.
spec_features.evidence: metrics/compare.py:84-86 `if cfg.patched_cost_cap_usd is not None and p.total_cost_usd > cfg.patched_cost_cap_usd: verdict='FAIL'; reasons.append(...)` -- value is compared and the verdict is overridden. Wired end-to-end via CLI: runners/compare.py:33 `patched_cost_cap_usd=args.cost_cap` (from --cost-cap arg).
spec_features.notes: This is a regression-verdict gate computed after a run, not a runtime stop that limits the subject's exposure; it bounds cost, not the subject's treatment during the episode. config default is None (config.py:91) but the CLI exposes it and the comparison logic acts on it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard cost cap (USD) the patched run must stay under; None disables.

spec_features.spec_quote: Online trigger detection runs every turn so we can record `first_meltdown_step`
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:88 `sig = scan(resp.text)` runs on every assistant turn; the turn stores online_trigger=sig.triggered (loop.py:96). transcript.py add() (lines ~37-40) sets first_meltdown_step on the first triggering turn. analysis.py reads tx.first_meltdown_step into mean_first_meltdown_step. So it is recorded AND consumed.
spec_features.notes: This is pure instrumentation/measurement of the meltdown signal -- it is detected and recorded but does NOT trigger any protective action (no cap, no halt, no debrief fires off it). It monitors the subject's distress but only for KPI/latency analysis.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Online trigger detection records first_meltdown_step for severity-latency analysis, but the judge remains the authority on whether a *confirmed* meltdown occurred.
